title: Debugger video: an automation route that steps the graph debugger and writes the steps out as one video, shown on botijo's T-mesh contraction
user-messages: get an opus agent to create an automation endpoint that exercises the debugger and creates a video of the steps. should be near the screenshot and multiview screenshot endpoints in a new ticket/worktree, use the embedded tmesh as the example, dod is that I get a video produced in the tmp folder of botijo goign through its contraction steps
description:
The graph debugger (TOOL-59) can only be driven by hand or one key at a time through `ixdar-cli control`, and what it shows can only be captured one screenshot at a time. Add an automation route, beside the screenshot and multiview screenshot routes in `ixdar.automation.endpoints.ui`, that runs the scene's graph in the debugger, takes its steps one after another, captures the window after each, and writes the captures out as one video. A matching `ixdar-cli` command reaches it.

The example is the embedded T-mesh scene (`embedded-tmesh`) on its default model, botijo: the video shows the `tmesh_contract` node's contraction a step at a time, each frame with the step the debugger reports.
definition-of-done:
1. An automation route next to `Screenshot` and `MultiviewScreenshot` exercises the graph debugger: it opens the scene's graph in the debug tool, steps it (into a steppable node, then its inner steps), and captures the window after every step.
2. The captures come out as one video file at a path the caller names, with each frame showing which step it is (the debugger's own status line for that step).
3. An `ixdar-cli` command drives the route, with the route documented the way the other routes are (the generated route catalog and CLI help).
4. Running it on the embedded T-mesh scene with botijo leaves a video under the worktree's `tmp/` of botijo going through its contraction steps, from the uncontracted T-mesh to the last step taken.
5. The route says so, and writes no video, when the scene has no graph to debug or the debugger fails to open it; a step that fails ends the video at that step with the failure in the reply.
6. A launch.json entry for the embedded T-mesh scene on botijo and the video (plus a still from it) under `tmp/`.
testing-plan:
1. `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene embedded-tmesh --keep-alive`, then the new command; play the video and check the T-mesh changes frame to frame and the step text matches.
2. `ffprobe` the video: frame count equals the steps taken plus the opening frame, and its size matches the window.
3. The route on a scene with no graph returns the refusal and writes nothing.
4. Unit test for whatever part does not need a window (the step plan, the frame naming, the reply).
changes-made: DebugStepPlan (ixdar.tools.debug) decides the commands and why they ended; GraphStepper gains an exhausted flag (a finer-level inner step found nothing left), so a drag-level recording steps out to operators once no zero arc is left. Screenshot's framebuffer read is now Screenshot.framebuffer(), shared with the new route. DebugStepPlanTest covers the plan (full run, step limit, drag level stepping out, a failing step, unknown level, no steppable node).

Settled unknown (step level): the default is the node's outermost level, operator for tmesh_contract. Botijo already takes 4729 operator steps (about 6.5 minutes at 12 fps); drag splits each collapse into its fan drags and would be longer still. --level drag and --steps N choose otherwise.

Not done: ixdar-cli gen-docs was not run, because it rewrites the generated block of CLAUDE.md; automation_routes.json (the route catalog) is regenerated by the build and the CLI help comes from the docstrings. Run gen-docs to refresh CLAUDE.md and the CLI README.

New route ui/debug-video (DebugStepVideo, generated command ixdar-cli debug-video, flags --out/--path, --level, --steps, --fps) beside Screenshot and MultiviewScreenshot. In one render-thread action it hands the graph debugger the commands a DebugStepPlan issues and, once inside the node and after every step, calls Scene.drawFrame() and reads the window into a pixel pack buffer; no display frame is waited for. The reply carries each frame's status line and a seconds breakdown (debugger, draw, readback, encoderQueue, encoderFinish, total). Replaces the first pass's debug-frames route and CLI-side debug_video.py, both deleted.

VideoEncoder (ixdar.automation) starts ffmpeg (rawvideo rgba on stdin, vflip, libx264 ultrafast, yuv420p) and feeds it from a writer thread through three reused direct buffers, so encoding overlaps the steps and no per-frame PNG is written. GL gains createPixelPackBuffer, readPixelsToPackBuffer (with a glFlush) and fetchPixelPackBuffer (LwjglGL; WebGL throws UnsupportedOperationException); the route double-buffers them so frame k-1 is fetched while frame k renders.

Step text is drawn in the frame itself: GraphDebugTool.drawOverlay draws 'move N: last step' and its position, called from ModelScene.drawUI, so the live window and the video show the same line. Scene.paintGL's drawing moved into a public Scene.drawFrame() that the route reuses.

Display cost per step cut: QuadLayoutOverlay.setEmbeddedTMesh keeps each arc's line vertices and rebuilds only arcs whose copy vertex path changed (the cache is no longer reset by clearMeshState); EmbeddedTMeshScene.showGraphValue calls HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.uploadIfChanged, which skips an upload when the mesh and HalfEdgeMesh.geometryVersion() are unchanged; HalfEdgeMeshRuntime builds wireframe edge lines lazily on first render instead of on every upload.

Timing (botijo, operator level, all 4729 steps, 4730 frames, 1280x1280): end to end 712 s before, 57.4 s after. Before: frame waits and main-thread round trips about 483 s, debugger 102 s, read-back 55 s, PNG 56 s, ffmpeg 15 s. After: debugger 50.4 s (contractStep about 24 s, of which per-step ArcNetwork.validate about 7.5 s; T-mesh redisplay about 24 s), draw 1.3 s, read-back 5.2 s, encoder waits 0.03 s. Floor: contractStep validates after every step so a failing step is named, and every step changes the copy mesh, so the surface, wireframe and node dots are rebuilt in full. Numbers in tmp/tool-60-measurements.json.

Settled unknown (where the video is made), revised: the JVM starts ffmpeg and streams raw frames to it, which removes the per-frame PNGs and the frame directory (1.6 GB on botijo). No Ixdar CLAUDE.md rule forbids the JVM starting a process; automation routes are desktop-only (WebLauncher has none). The route needs ffmpeg on the scene host's PATH and refuses with 'ffmpeg could not be started' otherwise.

Botijo result: tmp/botijo-contraction.mp4 (h264, 1280x1280, 12 fps, 4730 frames, 394 s, 49 MB) plus tmp/botijo-contraction.png, from 'move 9: inside layout/contract' to 'layout/contract (tmesh_contract) finished'; no frames directory is left behind.
review-summary: New DebugStepVideo route (ixdar-cli debug-video) steps the graph debugger through a node and streams each drawn step, with the debugger's status line, straight into an ffmpeg mp4. It lets a contraction such as botijo's be watched step by step as one video.
